title: Restriction and composition for locally closed extension by zero
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on the small pro-étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and inverse images of ring and module sheaves [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For a locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion, [def-weil-closed-immersion]), put $R_S=a^{-1}R$. For a factorization $a=v\circ c$ with $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ closed and $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ open [def-weil-open-immersion], set $a_!=v_!c_*$ on module sheaves, where $v_!$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the extension-by-zero presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] on the open slice site, equivalently the left adjoint to $v^{-1}$, and $c_*$ is direct image with its induced $R_V$-action. All coefficient rings on subschemes are inverse images of $R$. This functor is exact. Its termwise functor on unbounded derived categories is fully faithful and has a canonical natural isomorphism $a^*a_!\cong\mathrm{id}$, where $a^*$ is exact inverse image with the pulled-back coefficient ring. Restriction $a^*$ consequently induces a bijection
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(a_!M,a_!N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)
$$
for all $M,N\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},R_S)$.

The functor $a_!$ is independent of this factorization up to canonical isomorphisms restricting to the identity on $S$. If a factorization $a=i\circ u$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed is given, there is the same normalized identification $a_!\cong i_*u_!$. For locally closed immersions $b:T\hookrightarrow S$, there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$
\gamma_{a,b}:a_!b_!\xrightarrow{\sim}(a\circ b)_!,
$$
normalized to the identity after restriction to $T$. These identifications are unital and associative, on module sheaves and on their ordinary unbounded derived categories.

source.place: Composite consequence of proetale.tex: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion; Tag 09BM, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; Tag 09BN, lemma-open-immersion; Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open. Open extension is sites-modules.tex: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero; Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact. Composition of scheme immersions and its open-lifting construction are schemes.tex: Tag 02V0, lemma-composition-immersion. These passages give the open/closed factors; factorization independence and mixed composition are composite consequences, not verbatim assertions of one tag.

proof.text: Apply the normalized module-sheaf extension-system theorem to obtain exact functors, restriction comparisons, and normalized module composition satisfying the two unit laws and associativity. This result assumes neither full faithfulness nor a Hom bijection, on either module sheaves or derived categories.

Factor each coefficient immersion as a closed immersion followed by an open immersion. Mathlib IsImmersion.isImmersion_iff_exists supplies the factorization; the Noetherian-space subspace instance makes the intermediate scheme quasi-compact, and the inverse-image composition isomorphism specifies its coefficient identification. The coefficient equation is the isomorphism cancellation equation. Already on module sheaves, the separate open and closed adjunctions and restriction isomorphisms give full faithfulness of open extension and closed direct image. Transport along the closed comparison and gamma to deduce module full faithfulness for every locally closed immersion. Naturality gives that restriction conjugation followed by the extension map is the identity; full faithfulness gives the module Hom bijection. Descend each separate open or closed exact adjunction using the termwise complex adjunction and localization. The descended restriction isomorphism and adjunction show that open extension is fully faithful as a left adjoint and closed extension as a right adjoint. Transport closed full faithfulness along its specified comparison with actual direct image, and then use gamma for the closed/open factorization. Conjugating restriction by its natural isomorphism is bijective on Hom sets: its composite with the extension map is the identity by naturality, while full faithfulness makes extension a bijection.

Define derived restriction as the derived composite comparison followed by the derived identity comparison; define derived gamma by mapDerivedCategoryCompNatIso and derived identity by mapDerivedCategoryNatIso followed by the identity comparison. Their factorization formulas on Q of every complex are the exact-functor localization formulas. Derive the identity factorization formula from its homotopy-category factorization. For each unit law, derived natural-isomorphism transport respects postcomposition and eqToIso, and its whiskering and identity comparison equations convert the corresponding module unit law into the required derived law. For associativity apply the source library mapDerivedCategoryCompNatIso_cocycle to the module associativity equation, absorbing the final eqToIso into the last comparison, and use compatibility with postcomposition and equality transport to recover the required final eqToIso. These are complete Lean proofs of all fields of DerivedCoherence; there is no extra existence or boundedness assumption. Combine that constructed structure with the module-sheaf witness.
